ranking.note: Raised from P2: immediate-trim results entering peer reject filters blocks CPFP fee-bumping of trimmed package parents under mempool pressure, which is exactly the pinning/second-layer relay resistance this category ranks first.
Lowered from P2: a standardness relaxation that revisits a previously closed proposal with no cited downstream demand ranks below the correctness and DoS fixes held at P2 here.
Lowered from P3: narrow clock-skew edge case whose effect disappears entirely if #36540 lands, so it is redundant/marginal next to the other P3 fixes.
Lowered from P3: speculative policy for an unaccepted BIP, vendoring unmerged libsecp256k1 work; the mempool-policy portion cannot be evaluated until the consensus question is settled.

inconsistencies: #36540 (remove time-based expiry) and #36640 (clamp future mempool.dat entry times) address the same expiry mechanism; #36540 should be reviewed first, since merging it makes #36640 moot, and #36640 should not be merged ahead of that decision.

#36367 (clamp prioritisetransaction deltas) and #36538 (reject overflowing -bytespersigop, reorder sigop check) are two halves of the same class of problem — unbounded inputs overflowing cluster-mempool/fee arithmetic and tripping Assume aborts; reviewing them together would be more efficient than separately.

#35286 (testsubmitpackage, strict 1p1c dry-run) and #36608 (adds 1p1c package relay support to submitpackage) touch the same package-submission entry points; whichever lands first will force rework in the other, so sequence them deliberately.

#35581 consumes cluster-mempool fee-diagram chunk deltas, which #36367 shows can currently go negative through prioritisetransaction; #36367 should be settled first so the new notification is built on sound chunk fee data.
#36122 vendors unmerged experimental libsecp256k1 PRs and is declared by its author as not for merge; its mempool-policy content cannot be reviewed independently of the BIP460/458/459 process.
result.notes: Only one PR here reaches P1: the rest of the bug fixes (#36182, #35026, #36538, #36367) are real correctness/stability problems but each is bounded to reorgs, misconfiguration, or estimator readiness rather than ongoing relay censorship. Two policy-relaxation PRs (#36466, #29843) sit in P3 because neither cites external demand beyond developer/application convenience; the test-coverage PRs split by project relevance, with cluster-mempool reorg coverage (#36214) above the narrow Taproot reject-string checks (#35882).
